newsitem.title: USA: Toys R Us Q1 same-store toy sales up 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Toys R Us Q1 same-store toy sales up 8 pct.

text.p: Toys R Us Inc said Monday that comparable-store sales for its U.S. toy stores rose eight percent in the first quarter ended May 3, while comparable store sales decreased at Kids R Us and Babies R Us.
Toys R Us reported first quarter earnings of $0.10 a share on sales of $1.9 billion, compared to $0.07 a share on sales of $1.6 billion the previous first quarter.
The company said the toy store increases were driven by strong sales of video product, action figures, plush and outdoor playsets.
Sales decreases at Kids and Babies were primarily because of a weak demand for children's apparel and the effect of the transition of Baby Superstores to Babies R Us operations.

The company said it had double-digit comparable-store sales increases in Canada and the United Kingdom and that its stores in Japan, Central Europe, France, Spain, and Australia posted comparable store sales gains.

According to the company, these sales increases were driven by the continued success of the video business, spurred by the introduction of Nintendo 64 in most of Europe, as well as innovative marketing and advertising programs.
The first quarter results were helped by strong expense controls as well as lower interest expense from improved cash flow, the company said.
